record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: enumerating all stable matchings in smt
record.original_question: Does there exist an efficient output-sensitive algorithm that, given an instance I of Stable Marriage with Ties of size n, lists all stable matchings in time O(p(n) + |S_I| q(n)) for some polynomials p and q?

evidence.quote: it is an open problem as to whether there is an efficient algorithm for listing all stable matchings, given an instance I of smt of size n. By efficient, we mean that the algorithm should have complexity O(p(n) + |SI|q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage with Ties (SMT) problem consists of two disjoint sets of n men and n women, where each person ranks all members of the opposite sex in a preference list that is a weak linear order (i.e., ties among equally preferred partners are allowed). A matching M is a bijection between the men and the women. Given a matching M, a pair (m,w) not in M is said to be a blocking pair for M (under the weak-dominance / weak stability notion) if m strictly prefers w to his partner in M and w strictly prefers m to her partner in M. A matching is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. Let S_I denote the set of all weakly stable matchings of an SMT instance I of size n.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given any SMT instance I of size n, outputs every matching in S_I (each exactly once) in total running time O(p(n) + |S_I| · q(n)) for some fixed polynomials p and q?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of enumerating all weakly stable matchings in an SMT instance with output-sensitive (polynomial-delay or total polynomial in n + |S_I|) complexity appears to remain open. While the Irving–Leather algorithm gives such an enumeration for the classical Stable Marriage problem (without ties), no analogous output-sensitive algorithm is known for SMT, and surveys of open problems in matching under preferences continue to list this question as unresolved. No evidence of a resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: A Study of Stable Marriage Problems With Ties (Scott)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses enumeration of stable matchings under ties; notes complexity challenges introduced by ties.
status_evidence.claim: Enumerating stable matchings in SMT is computationally more challenging than the classical case, with no known output-sensitive algorithm cited.

status_evidence.title: Stable matching problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the lattice of stable matchings and Irving–Leather enumeration for the tie-free case.
status_evidence.claim: Output-sensitive enumeration is known for the tie-free Stable Marriage problem via Irving–Leather, but the article does not present an analog for SMT.
